question.text: Per the chapter, terminal growth rates for 'consolidated industries' in DCF are normally considered at:

explanation.text: The Logic: Per the chapter: 'Normally terminal growth rates for consolidated industries are considered at 2-3% above the inflation rate.' This is the baseline reference point used in DCF for mature, consolidated sectors. The Trap: 8-10% above inflation overstates a sustainable perpetuity rate for a mature industry; the risk-free rate is too low; equating terminal growth to GDP in all cases ignores sector-specific maturity. Note: The workbook ties the 2-3%-above-inflation reference specifically to consolidated industries; higher-growth or sunrise sectors may justify different assumptions.
